name: Gooseberry
grown_as: A fruit bush, usually on a short leg. William grows 'Hinnonmäki Red' and 'Hinnonmäki Green', both mildew-resistant Finnish varieties; they differ only in fruit colour. The drawing shows the red one. ⚠️ CHECK which colour to draw
habit: A spreading, rather untidy deciduous shrub, 1 to 1.5 m, with arching branches. Sharp spines, one to three together, just below each leaf or leaf cluster. Fruit on spurs and at the base of last year's shoots.

leaf.arrangement: Alternate on young shoots; in small clusters on the spurs
leaf.outline: Small and roundish, 2 to 5 cm across, with three to five rounded lobes
leaf.margin: Large, rounded, blunt teeth (scalloped) along the outer part of each lobe
leaf.veins: Three to five main veins fanning from the stalk
leaf.surface: Slightly downy, dull to faintly glossy mid green; paler beneath
leaf.colour: Mid green, often yellowish in autumn

flower.form: A small hanging bell with its five sepals swept back
flower.petals: Five small upright whitish petals inside, shorter than the sepals; the five sepals, joined into a short tube then curled sharply back, make the show
flower.colour: Sepals reddish-purple to pink-flushed green; petals white
flower.centre: Five stamens and a two-lobed style poking out from the mouth
flower.behind: A green, often bristly, rounded ovary above the bell, which becomes the berry
flower.carried: One to three together, hanging below the shoot on short stalks from the leaf clusters

fruit: A round to oval berry, 1.5 to 3 cm, translucent, with pale lines running from end to end, smooth or with a few bristles and with a dry brown tuft of old flower at the tip. 'Hinnonmäki Red' ripens dark red; 'Hinnonmäki Green' stays green to yellow-green. Hangs singly or in twos under the branches. June to July.
seedling: Not drawn: grown from cuttings or bought plants
winter: Bare arching grey-brown stems with sharp spines at each node and small pointed buds.

leaf: small roundish leaf with three to five rounded lobes
bloom: a small hanging flower with reddish sepals swept sharply back
small white petals and stamens poking from the mouth
flower: small flowers hanging singly or in twos below the shoots
crop: veined translucent berries hanging singly under spiny branches

look_alikes: Currants have no spines and carry their flowers and fruit on long strings. Jostaberry is spineless with bigger leaves and black fruit in small clusters.
